status: mechanism_only - use_output_fusion=False in every arm, so the LLM reaches the GNN ONLY through the consultative feedback path. NOT comparable to results/unsw_nb15_current.json (fusion on).
question: Does edge injection (--injection-mode edge, the canonical default) still causally use the LLM's advice under v2 encoding and the canonical top_k/scale (31.0/2.0), now that the loop-fusion fairness fix has landed? Supersedes results/unsw_nb15_edge_injection.json, which was measured pre-v2 under a different mechanism-only variant.
verdict: YES. real > control_head_only > control_shuffled > control_random, on both UNSW and ToN-IoT. The gain is small (+0.0064 UNSW, +0.0026 ToN) and sits inside one seed's noise band, so treat it as directional, not decisive -- but the 4-arm ordering is clean on both datasets, including ToN, where the pre-v2 mechanism-only test did not separate real from random advice.

arms.control_head_only: feedback structurally absent (bias term not added); the correct no-mechanism baseline, never the bare GNN rung
arms.real: true whitened-prototype advice delivered to the consulted edge
arms.control_shuffled: real advice delivered to the WRONG edge
arms.control_random: fixed uniform noise in place of advice

pass_criterion: real > control_head_only AND both advice controls <= control_head_only. Met on both datasets.
reproduce: scratchpad script mechanism_only_v2.py (session-local, not checked into the repo); raw per-arm output preserved at mechanism_only_v2.json alongside it.

supersedes.reason: That file measured a different mechanism-only variant (edge_prototype/edge_trained_head/attention arms, pre-v2 encoding, injection_scale swept 10-100) and is not re-verified on v2. This file is the v2, canonical-top_k/scale, 4-control-arm re-run, on both datasets.

caveats: 3-seed means; std 0.01-0.03 on both datasets, so the real-vs-control point gain (+0.006 UNSW, +0.003 ToN) is smaller than one seed's noise band. The ordering across all 4 arms, not the magnitude of the top gap, is the load-bearing evidence here.

control_random has by far the highest churn (0.042 UNSW, 0.109 ToN) yet the lowest score -- noise perturbs predictions the most while making them worse, which is itself evidence the mechanism is not simply capacity-limited.
Not comparable to results/unsw_nb15_current.json or results/ton_iot_current.json: those runs have output fusion ON, this experiment has it OFF in every arm by design.
